questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the right first question when deciding whether to use a multimodal call?
options: Can the model technically accept images or audio?
Which provider has the cheapest multimodal pricing this month?
Does the task actually require the raw modality, or can it be reduced to text first?
Is multimodal input currently trending in the industry?
questions.explain: Most frontier models can technically accept images or audio — the real question is whether the task needs the raw modality or can be converted to text first.

questions.q: What is the 'convert-first' pattern described in this lesson?
options: Always sending raw images directly to the most expensive model available
Converting every text request into an image before sending it
Running two different vision models on the same image for verification
Extracting text from an image or audio source once (e.g. via OCR), then reasoning over that text repeatedly instead of resending the raw media
questions.explain: Convert-first means paying the modality cost once (e.g. OCR on a receipt), then reusing the resulting text for every subsequent reasoning step, instead of repeatedly sending raw media.

questions.q: Which scenario is the clearest example of a task where multimodal input earns its cost?
options: Summarizing a UI mockup, where the visual layout itself is the information
Reading the total off a receipt that will be referenced many times afterward
Answering a user's plain typed support question
Processing a web page whose HTML/text is already available
questions.explain: When the layout or appearance itself carries the needed information (like a mockup's design), there's no text substitute without losing exactly what matters — that's when multimodal is worth it.

questions.q: How does this lesson extend Lesson 11's cost/latency/quality framework?
options: It replaces that framework with a completely different one for multimodal tasks
It applies the same cost/latency/quality trade-off thinking to the choice of modality, not just the choice of model
It argues cost and latency no longer matter once multimodal models exist
It claims multimodal calls are always cheaper than text-only calls
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly reuses Lesson 11's framework: text-only is cheapest/fastest, multimodal costs more but can do tasks text-only simply cannot — the same trade-off logic, applied to modality.

questions.q: Why does a high-volume pipeline benefit from converting a scanned receipt to text once rather than re-sending the image on every follow-up turn?
options: Because images cannot be used more than once in any API
Because OCR is always 100% accurate and multimodal models are not
Because the vision cost is paid once, and every subsequent reasoning step then uses a cheaper, faster text-only call
Because text-only models have no token costs at all
questions.explain: Paying the (higher) vision cost once and reusing the extracted text for every later reasoning step avoids repeatedly paying the modality cost on every turn.
